title: How coffee conquered the world
text: Coffee's rise from Ethiopian legend to global habit is a story of trade and obsession. By the seventeenth century, coffee houses had become centres of {{1}} (POLITICS) debate; some rulers briefly banned them, fearing revolution. Coffee's stimulating effect comes from caffeine, a natural chemical the plant produces for its own {{2}} (PROTECT). Today, coffee is grown in over seventy countries and supports the {{3}} (LIVE) of some 125 million people. Yet the industry faces an uncertain future: rising temperatures are making traditional growing regions less {{4}} (SUIT). Scientists are developing more {{5}} (RESIST) varieties, though purists complain about the taste. Coffee drinkers remain fiercely {{6}} (LOYAL) to their favourite blends. For millions of people, the morning cup is simply {{7}} (DISPENSE) — a small daily ritual. Few products can match its combination of {{8}} (POPULAR) and profitability.

gaps.explanation: 'for its own protection' — noun from protect.
'fiercely loyal' — the adjective keeps the base form.
'its combination of popularity and profitability' — noun forms of both adjectives.
